statement_record.book: A preordered set is a category with at most one arrow x -> y; an adjunction F -| U between preorders P, Q is exactly a pair of monotone maps satisfying the two-way rule Fa <= x iff a <= Ux (the hom-set iso degenerating to a bi-implication of propositions), i.e. a Galois connection; the unit at p is p <= UFp with UFp least among the Ux satisfying p <= Ux, dually FUq <= q with FUq greatest among the Fy <= q.
statement_record.intree: [Proset] turns any [PreOrder R] into a Category whose hom is R itself and whose hom-setoid is the trivial [equiv _ _ := True], so the category is thin (all parallel arrows equal, hom = mere proposition); [Adjunction] is the hom-setoid isomorphism (F x ~> y) ≊ (x ~> U y) with the four naturality fields, and [unit]/[counit] are ⌊id⌋ / ⌈id⌉.
statement_record.strength_comparison: same for the two ingredients taken separately (preorder-as-thin-category, and adjunction as the hom-set bijection, which over a [Proset] IS Awodey's bicondition because both hom-setoids are subsingletons); intree-weaker in that the SPECIALIZATION is never taken: no in-tree constant instantiates [Adjunction] at a [Proset], and the least/greatest characterizations of the unit/counit are only available in their general form (the universal-arrow UMP), never restated in order-theoretic language.

statement_record.book: In a preorder all propositional structure is given by adjoint two-way rules: meets (r <= p/\q iff r<=p and r<=q), joins (p\/q<=r iff p<=r and q<=r), Heyting implication as an exponential (p/\q<=r iff p<=q=>r), and 0 <= p <= 1; hence Heyting algebra is formulable entirely by adjoints, and these adjoint rules of inference form a complete sequent calculus for intuitionistic propositional logic. Negation ~p := (p => 0) yields contraposition (from q |- ~p infer p |- ~q); adding ~~p |- p gives classical logic.
statement_record.intree: [Props] is the thin category of Prop with hom := Basics.impl and the trivial hom-setoid, carrying [Props_Terminal] (True), [Props_Initial] (False), [Props_Cartesian] (and), [Props_Cocartesian] (or) and [Props_Closed] (impl); the exponential UMP is the field `exp_iso {x y z} : x × y ~> z ≊ x ~> z^y` and the product UMP the biconditional [ump_products].
statement_record.strength_comparison: same for the four adjoint rules — the in-tree UMPs are proof-relevant biconditionals/isos that degenerate exactly to Awodey's bi-implications in a thin category, and Props instantiates all of them; intree-weaker in that there is no abstract HeytingAlgebra notion, negation/contraposition/classical extension are not developed, and the metatheoretic completeness claim about the sequent calculus has no counterpart.

Definition representable_adjunction : (F ⊣ U) ↔ (Repr_left F ≅[[D^op ∏ C, Sets]] Repr_right U) := (adjunction_to_repr_iso, repr_iso_to_adjunction).  (Both directions Defined: adjunction_to_repr_iso at line 57, repr_iso_to_adjunction at line 64.)
Class Representable `(F : C ⟶ Sets) := { repr_obj : C; represented : [Hom repr_obj,─] ≅ F }.

statement_record.book: Reading Corollary 9.17 backwards: for any functor f : C -> D of small categories the composite f* o y_D : D -> C-hat = Sets^(C^op), d |-> Hom_D(f-, d), is an adjoint to f, so in this sense every functor has an adjoint; the caveat is that its values are presheaves ('ideal elements') rather than objects of C, and the honest adjoint on C exists only when those values happen to be representable.
statement_record.intree: The functor the remark constructs exists in-tree in uncurried form: [Repr_left F : C ⇸ D] is Hom D ◯ (F^op ∏⟶ Id), i.e. (c, d) ↦ D(F c, d), which is precisely f* ∘ y_D read as a bifunctor C^op ∏ D ⟶ Sets; its counterpart [Repr_right U] is (c, d) ↦ C(c, U d). The remark's caveat has an in-tree cousin in [representable_adjunction] : (F ⊣ U) ↔ (Repr_left F ≅ Repr_right U), the statement that an honest adjoint U is exactly a witness that the profunctor D(F−,−) is represented in the form C(−, U−); pointwise representability itself is the class [Representable] of Functor/Representable.v.
statement_record.strength_comparison: intree-weaker: the object is present but nothing is CLAIMED of it. [Repr_left f] is never curried into a functor D ⟶ [C^op, Sets], is never called an adjoint of f in any sense (there is no Prof bicategory, no relative/pro-adjoint notion, and no free-cocompletion in-tree), and [representable_adjunction] quantifies over an ALREADY GIVEN U rather than asserting 'an adjoint exists iff the values D(f−, d) are representable' — the existential form, which is the remark's actual punchline, is not stated and would additionally need the pointwise [Representable] witnesses assembled into a functor.

gap: Three things are missing. (1) CURRYING: no in-tree constant presents Awodey's adjoint as a functor D ⟶ [C^op, Sets]; Theory/Profunctor.v:155 gives only the uncurried bifunctor Repr_left f : C^op ∏ D ⟶ Sets, and the tree has no hom-tensor currying [C^op ∏ D, Sets] ≅ [D, [C^op, Sets]]. (2) THE ADJOINTNESS CLAIM: nothing states that Repr_left f is an adjoint of f in any sense — there is no bicategory of profunctors (Theory/Profunctor.v builds composition and the unit/associator laws in Construction/Profunctor/{Compose,Laws}.v but no Prof bicategory instance and no adjunctions in it), and no notion of an adjoint valued in a free cocompletion. (3) THE REPRESENTABILITY CRITERION AS AN EXISTENCE TEST: [representable_adjunction] (Theory/Profunctor/Adjunction.v:70) presupposes a given U; the remark's 'the honest adjoint exists only when these values are representable' — i.e. (∃ U, f ⊣ U) ↔ ∀ d, Representable (Repr_left f (−, d)) — is not stated, and Functor/Representable.v's [Representable] class is never connected to adjoints anywhere in the tree (verified by grepping every use of repr_obj/represented).
